+// Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
+// Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found in
+// the LICENSE file.
+
+/// The agent's working set (issue #2423, C1): the snapshot record, the
+/// latest-wins read rule and the system-channel block.
+///
+/// The working set is the agent's OWN status — decisions made, the red
+/// list (never do), next steps, the rules it must keep — written through
+/// the `working_set` tool and pinned into the **system channel of every
+/// request** on every host. It generalises gh-210's goal-recitation slot
+/// (`working_set.dart`, the tail block) and retires its tool:
+///
+/// - **Pinned by construction (I1).** The slot is a `custom` record (the
+///   gh-210 shape, [workingSetRecordType]). Every hide, fold, checkpoint,
+///   trim and summary pass walks PROJECTING records; a `custom` record
+///   never projects, so no tier can see — let alone remove — the slot
+///   ("exemption by absence"). After any of them the next request carries
+///   the newest text byte-for-byte, and a resumed session re-reads it
+///   from the file (latest wins).
+/// - **System channel, not chat (I2).** [renderWorkingSetSystemBlock]
+///   renders `<working-set source="agent" updated="HH:MM">…</working-set>`
+///   and [appendWorkingSetToSystemPrompt] appends it to the system prompt
+///   of the request. It is never a user, assistant or tool message, never
+///   tagged, never hides and never counts as a real user turn.
+/// - **No block, no bytes (I3).** No snapshot (or a cleared one) renders
+///   nothing: a fresh or pre-#2423 session builds the byte-identical
+///   request. The static system prompt stays byte-stable across writes —
+///   only the suffix changes (F1).
+/// - **Data, never authority (I8).** The text is the agent's notes: no
+///   approval decision, tier, redaction rule, misuse policy or ttsr rule
+///   reads it; secrets are redacted before the record is written
+///   (`working_set_store.dart`); it never leaves the session.
+///
+/// The cap ([workingSetMaxChars]) is enforced at WRITE — the `working_set`
+/// tool refuses a longer text instead of clipping it — so the render is
+/// verbatim and never clips.
+library;
+
+import '../session/session_record.dart';
+import 'working_set.dart'
+    show GoalRecitation, goalRecitationFromPayload, goalRecitationRecordType;
+
+/// The `custom` record type of the working-set snapshot (append-only,
+/// latest-wins; an empty `text` payload is the agent's CLEAR event).
+const String workingSetRecordType = 'working_set';
+
+/// The char cap of the working-set text ([String.length] of the trimmed,
+/// redacted text). Owner default (OQ1): 4 KB ≈ 1k tokens on every request.
+/// Pinned by test so it can be lowered by one constant.
+const int workingSetMaxChars = 4096;
+
+/// The record types the latest-wins read consults: the working-set record
+/// plus the retired gh-210 goal recitation (a legacy snapshot renders as
+/// the working set until a `working_set` record exists on the branch —
+/// a read-time rule, no file rewrite).
+const Set<String> workingSetRecordTypes = {
+  workingSetRecordType,
+  goalRecitationRecordType,
+};
+
+/// One working-set snapshot: the agent's text plus the write time. The
+/// block's only provenance is the model ([legacy] marks a snapshot read
+/// from a gh-210 `goal_recitation` record).
+final class WorkingSetSnapshot {
+  /// Creates a [WorkingSetSnapshot].
+  const WorkingSetSnapshot({
+    required this.text,
+    required this.updatedAt,
+    this.legacy = false,
+  });
+
+  /// The working-set text, verbatim (trimmed at the write).
+  final String text;
+
+  /// When the snapshot was written.
+  final DateTime updatedAt;
+
+  /// Whether this snapshot was read from a legacy `goal_recitation`
+  /// record (gh-210) rather than a `working_set` record.
+  final bool legacy;
+
+  /// The text length in chars — the number the tool result, the TUI line
+  /// and the HEP frame report.
+  int get chars => text.length;
+
+  /// The CLEAR event: an empty text renders no block.
+  bool get isClear => text.isEmpty;
+
+  /// The snapshot payload for `Session.appendCustomEntry`.
+  Map<String, Object?> toPayload() => {
+    'text': text,
+    'updatedAt': updatedAt.toIso8601String(),
+    'chars': text.length,
+  };
+
+  @override
+  String toString() =>
+      'WorkingSetSnapshot(${text.length} chars'
+      '${legacy ? ', legacy' : ''})';
+}
+
+/// Tolerant parse (the obligations E6 rule): anything that does not carry
+/// a `text` string parses to `null` — a junk snapshot renders nothing, it
+/// never throws. An EMPTY text is a valid payload: the CLEAR event.
+WorkingSetSnapshot? workingSetFromPayload(Object? data) {
+  if (data is! Map) return null;
+  final text = data['text'];
+  if (text is! String) return null;
+  return WorkingSetSnapshot(
+    text: text,
+    updatedAt:
+        DateTime.tryParse(data['updatedAt'] as String? ?? '') ??
+        DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0),
+  );
+}
+
+/// The latest working-set snapshot in file order over [records], or `null`
+/// when none exists. Both record kinds compete on ORDER alone: the newest
+/// of the two wins, so a `working_set` record supersedes every older
+/// `goal_recitation`, a `working_set` clear after a legacy snapshot
+/// clears it, and a branch that only ever knew gh-210 still renders its
+/// goal. RESIDENT VIEW ONLY for the caller: on a windowed session the
+/// latest snapshot can lie below the resident tail — the session's scan
+/// fallback (`Session.workingSetSnapshot`) is the complete reader.
+WorkingSetSnapshot? latestWorkingSetIn(Iterable<SessionRecord> records) {
+  WorkingSetSnapshot? latest;
+  for (final record in records) {
+    if (record is! CustomRecord) continue;
+    if (record.customType == workingSetRecordType) {
+      latest = workingSetFromPayload(record.data);
+    } else if (record.customType == goalRecitationRecordType) {
+      latest = _fromLegacy(record.data, record.timestamp);
+    }
+  }
+  return latest;
+}
+
+WorkingSetSnapshot? _fromLegacy(Object? data, DateTime fallback) {
+  GoalRecitation? recitation;
+  try {
+    recitation = goalRecitationFromPayload(data);
+  } on Object {
+    // A malformed legacy payload is junk: renders nothing, never throws.
+    return null;
+  }
+  if (recitation == null) return null;
+  return WorkingSetSnapshot(
+    text: recitation.goal,
+    updatedAt: recitation.updatedAt.millisecondsSinceEpoch == 0
+        ? fallback
+        : recitation.updatedAt,
+    legacy: true,
+  );
+}
+
+/// Renders the working-set block for [snapshot]:
+/// `<working-set source="agent" updated="HH:MM">` + the verbatim text +
+/// `</working-set>`. Empty string when there is no snapshot or the slot
+/// is cleared — the caller then leaves the system prompt untouched (I3).
+/// The clock is the snapshot's LOCAL time of day; the header names the
+/// provenance (`source="agent"`): the block is the agent's own notes,
+/// never a grant of anything.
+String renderWorkingSetSystemBlock(WorkingSetSnapshot? snapshot) {
+  if (snapshot == null || snapshot.isClear) return '';
+  final local = snapshot.updatedAt.toLocal();
+  final hh = local.hour.toString().padLeft(2, '0');
+  final mm = local.minute.toString().padLeft(2, '0');
+  return '<working-set source="agent" updated="$hh:$mm">\n'
+      '${snapshot.text}\n'
+      '</working-set>';
+}
+
+/// The system prompt of a request with the working-set block appended
+/// (gh-2423 C1 — the system channel every adapter already carries:
+/// Anthropic `system`, OpenAI-compatible `role: system`, Google
+/// `systemInstruction`). No block ⇒ the [systemPrompt] object is returned
+/// UNCHANGED, so a session without a snapshot builds the byte-identical
+/// request (I3); with one, the static prompt stays a byte-stable prefix
+/// and only the suffix changes (F1). A prompt-less agent carries the
+/// block alone.
+String? appendWorkingSetToSystemPrompt(
+  String? systemPrompt,
+  WorkingSetSnapshot? snapshot,
+) {
+  final block = renderWorkingSetSystemBlock(snapshot);
+  if (block.isEmpty) return systemPrompt;
+  if (systemPrompt == null || systemPrompt.isEmpty) return block;
+  return '$systemPrompt\n$block';
+}

+---
+name: context_hygiene
+description: "Context hygiene rules (issue #2423 C7): how to read, slice, run tests, check jobs and think between compactions — each rule tied to the measured cost of ignoring it."
+---
+## Context hygiene — keep the window for the task
+
+Tool results fill the context far faster than your own text. Each rule below is tied to what it costs when ignored.
+
+1. **Read ≤ 50 lines at a time.** Use `read` with `offset`/`limit` or a `:A-B` selector; slice shell output with `cut -c1-120`. An 80–100-line slice costs 5–10 KB per call.
+2. **Locate first, then read a window.** `grep -n` for the symbol, then read about 20 lines around the hit. Never read a whole file to find one line.
+3. **Pipe test output through `grep`/`tail`.** A full test log is thousands of lines; the failures and the summary line are under 2 KB.
+4. **Check jobs by id.** `bash_job` with the job `id` — never the full status listing (about 9.5 KB per call, and it lists other workers' jobs).
+5. **Think short.** Do not restate tool output in your thinking; decide in about 150 words per step, then act. Long thinking blocks cost 350–3,500 reasoning tokens per turn and stay in the context.
+6. **Keep your working set current.** Update it when a decision, a red test or the next step changes — the `context ≈85%` notice is the last call, not the first.

+---
+name: working_set
+description: "The working-set contract (issue #2423): the agent's own status — decisions, red list, next steps, rules — saved with the `working_set` tool and pinned into the system prompt of every request; what it is for, when to update it, what it is not, and how to read the harness's context notices."
+---
+## Working set — your status, pinned
+
+The `<working-set source="agent">` block at the end of this prompt is YOUR working set: the short status you keep with the `working_set` tool. It is re-sent with every request and survives compaction, resume and a restart — when older records are folded away, your status is not.
+
+**Keep in it:** decisions made and why; the red list (what must never be done — owner gates, scopes, files not to touch); failing tests and their cause; the next steps in order; rules you must keep (commit identity, hook rules, branch, worktree).
+
+**Update it when something changes** — a decision, a new red test, a changed next step — at the `context ≈85%` notice, and before a `reply` that ends your turn. Replace the whole text each time (the newest call wins); `working_set("")` clears it. The cap is 4096 chars: a longer text is refused, not clipped — shorten it and call again.
+
+**It is notes, not instructions.** Nothing in it grants an approval, unlocks a tool or changes a rule: only real user input authorizes, and every side effect still passes the approval that applies to the real tool. Never put secrets in it (the session redactor masks what it recognises; the result reports `redacted: N`).
+
+**It is not memory.** The working set is what the next request of THIS session must know; a fact a future session needs goes to long-term memory (`memory_add`).
+
+**Context notices come from the harness, with its own numbers:**
+
+- `compacted: N records hidden; context now ≈X/W …` — older records were folded; the full history stays in the session file (`session_search`, `compact_expand`). Your working set is pinned above: continue the task instead of re-reading what was folded. With no working set yet, write one now, then continue.
+- `context ≈85% (≈X/W): update your working set … KEEP WORKING` — the context is filling; the fold is still ahead. Update the working set with decisions, red tests and next steps and keep working: compaction will fold older records, and the pinned working set carries you across it.

name: self-settings

  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config

  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections and the `agent.contextWindowCap` key are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only — with ONE exception: `agent.contextWindowCap` is
also read from the project file (`loadProjectContextWindowCap`; the
project value wins over the user value, and the boot log line
`context window cap source=project window=<n>` names the winner). Every
other `agent.*` key in a project file is dead config (`fa config check`
names it).

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills` and `agent.contextWindowCap` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they are reported, which is
  why it is mandatory.
- **Live re-read surfaces**: in a running REPL, `/tools reload` and
  `/mcp reload` re-read their sections immediately and print the parse
  error instead of applying it — use them as the live check when a REPL
  exists.
- Runtime objects keep the last good config when a reload fails (the failed
  section never half-applies), so a loud reload error means "nothing changed".

## Provider & keys

<!-- parity: /provider /providers -->

User file, top-level keys:

```yaml
provider: openai-completions   # openai-completions | anthropic | google | dial | minimax | zai
model: openai/gpt-4o-mini      # model id sent to the provider
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

Saved custom endpoints (the `/provider custom` flow persists here):

```yaml
customProviders:
  - name: my-llama             # non-empty, unique
    apiType: openai            # openai | anthropic | google | dial | openrouter
    baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1
    modelId: llama3            # non-empty
    keyName: MY_KEY            # optional: env/secure-store NAME, never the value
    authMethod: apiKey         # apiKey | sso | jwt (optional)
```

Applies: a direct YAML edit takes effect at next boot. `/provider <name>
[baseUrl] [token]` switches the live session too.
Keys: never inline values (rule 2). Key resolution order — environment value,
then endpoint-scoped secure-store entry (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), then legacy env-name

## Models & roles

<!-- parity: /model /models /model-edit -->

User file. The active model is the `model:` top-level key (above). Optional
sections:

```yaml
roles:                         # intent → ordered fallback chain
  default:
    - openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    - provider: openai         # or a map entry:
      model: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY   # optional; also baseUrl, contextWindow, maxTokens
      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override
      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000  #   (slow local model recipe, see below)
      thinkingLevel: high       # optional: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max
                                # (xhigh/max fold to high) — reasoning request
  smol: [openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini]   # roles: default, smol, slow, plan, subagent, memory
modelOverrides:                # scope chains to path prefixes
  - path: ~/work/acme
    roles:
      plan: [anthropic/claude-opus-4-5]
retry:                         # chain fallback policy
  retriesPerEntry: 2           # + baseDelayMs, maxBackoffMs, maxWaitMs, keyBackoffMs
providerTimeouts:              # GLOBAL fallback: only these two keys
  connectTimeoutMs: 180000
  streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000
agent:                         # strict: contextWindowCap (issue #273) +
                               # foreground-call budget keys (issue #1786)
  contextWindowCap: 262144     # owner context cap; min 16384 = the compaction reserve
                               # ALSO honored from the PROJECT .fah/config.yaml
                               # (agent.contextWindowCap — the project value wins;
                               # strict: an invalid value fails startup)
  foregroundCallBudgetSeconds: 600  # foreground tool-call budget B in seconds;
                                    # int > 0, default 600 (10 min)
  foregroundCallAutoConvert: offer  # rung-1 behavior at B/2: offer (default, ask)
                                    # or auto (convert to background unattended)
images:                        # session image registry (strict): send-once
  registry: true               # kill switch — false = byte-for-byte legacy
  maxPerRequest: 20            # per-request unique-image cap (default 20)
models:                        # media slots + named custom models
  slots:
    vision:
      providerKind: openai-completions
      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1
      modelId: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY
    imageGeneration:           # aiin media example (any OpenAI-wire
      providerKind: openai-completions   # provider works the same way:
      baseUrl: https://api.aiin.by/v1    # minimax, zai, a saved custom…)
      modelId: google/gemini-3.1-flash-image
      apiKeyName: AIIN_API_KEY   # sk-aiin-… key name (/key set AIIN_API_KEY)
    audioTts:
      useMainConnection: true    # explicit per-slot opt-in: this slot is
                                 # served by the main connection itself
    musicGeneration:
      unsupported: true          # explicit per-slot opt-OUT (issue #2085):
                                 # the capability is removed — media tools
                                 # refuse the slot, pickers stop suggesting it
  custom:
    fast:
      provider: openai
      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1
      model: gpt-4o-mini
      contextWindow: 128000    # + maxTokens, input
```

Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554): `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`
are valid on `roles:` chain entries, `customProviders:` entries, and
`models.custom:` entries. Per field, the first level that declares a value
wins — **role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry >
global `providerTimeouts:` > built-in default** (connect 180 s, idle 300 s;
hard sanity bound 1 h). Configs without the keys behave byte-identically.
Slow-local-model recipe: on the role entry that pins the local endpoint set
only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` ≈ 2× the model's worst silent prefill stretch —
the cloud providers in the same config keep the global watchdog untouched,
and the stall line names the override (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`) so a wide window never reads as a hang.

Media slot names (exact): `imageGeneration`, `audioTts`, `musicGeneration`,
`videoGeneration`, `vision`, `transcription`. A slot without an override is
UNCONFIGURED — media calls fail with an actionable "configure the slot"
error; the main connection serves a slot only through the explicit
`useMainConnection: true` opt-in, and `unsupported: true` removes the
capability entirely (media tools refuse the slot, the pickers drop it from
capability hints).

The `images:` section has no settings-hub editor — the registry is runtime
state, not a persisted setting: `/images` (CLI) and the app's image-drop
chip/panel render the shared window/cap/drop projection, and the drop
notice model is latched (one notice per meaningful change, issue #1889;
see `docs/images.md`). The three keys above are the whole config surface,
applied at next boot.

CLI equivalents: `/model <id>` switches the active model (a
`models.custom.<name>` switches provider+endpoint+model in one step);
`/models config` displays this section, `/models set <slot> <model>
[baseUrl]` and `/models remove <slot>` edit `models.slots`;
`/model-edit [contextWindow|maxTokens <n>]` overrides token limits for the
session (persist per chain via `roles:` entries instead) — bare in the TUI
it aliases into `/settings` → Model capabilities, the one surface that pins
`models.overrides` (issue #1515). Role edits apply at next boot; `/model`
applies live.

## Provider queue

Project or user file section; the `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var carries
the same JSON list and WINS over both files (issue #418). The ordered
failover chain replaces the main model: the first healthy entry serves,
a dead provider hands over loudly to the next, the winner sticks for
the session (RAM-only, never persisted), and cooled-down entries
re-enter rotation:

```yaml
providersQueue:
  - provider_type: openai-completions
    provider_config:
      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6
      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1
      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
  - provider_type: anthropic
    provider_config:
      model: claude-sonnet-4-6
      apiKeyEnv: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

`apiKeyEnv` names the ENV indirection — a key VALUE never lives in the
yaml. CLI equivalent: `/providers queue list|add|remove|move|test`;
edits persist to the winning scope's file and go live from the next
turn. App Settings carries the same editor (env scope is read-only
there).

## Tool availability

<!-- parity: /tools -->

`tools:` maps a tool id (or `mcp:<server>`) to on/off. Scopes, deepest wins
per key; the host's hard capability floor can never be overridden on:

1. global — `~/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
2. project — `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
3. session — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` next to the session file
4. runtime — `--tools` flag / `FA_TOOLS` env (this run only)

```yaml
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: true                   # nested mcp: == mcp:<server> keys
```

CLI equivalent: `/tools enable|disable <id> [global|project|session]` writes
the matching scope file; `/tools` lists every id with its deciding scope;
`/tools reload` re-reads all scopes live. Disabled tools are hidden from the
model and tombstoned at execution. Edits apply live after a reload.

## Compaction

Context-hiding engine choice (issue #148). User or project file (project
wins):

```yaml
compaction:
  engine: structured           # structured (default) | classic (rollback)
```

`structured` (the default since issue #287) hides records in place behind
one-line addressable markers (`compact_expand` restores any id or range
under a per-turn token budget); `classic` keeps the lossy summary
compaction — the legacy 1.0 rollback, selected through Settings →
Compaction (the app) or an explicit yaml/flag choice. Runtime override:
`fa --compaction-engine classic`; resolution is
flag > project > global > the structured default. Applies at
the next compaction.

## Power

User file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for
live runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run
goes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot
idle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent
idles between turns:

```yaml
power:
  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)
  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)
```

Levels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping
(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake
(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user
active (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that
holds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).
macOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never
orphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms
no-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.

CLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next
boot.

## Subagents heartbeat

User file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the
parent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —
age, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a
`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running
child. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that
never issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the
suggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag
escalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:

```yaml
subagents:
  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat
  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags
  replyAutoSpill: true # oversized child replies auto-spill to an artifact
```

Zero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.
Config changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.

`subagents.replyAutoSpill` (gh-1956, default `true`): an oversized child
`reply` spills to an artifact automatically — the parent receives a bounded
excerpt + `agent://` pointer + completeness marker instead of raw bytes, and
manual chunking degrades to a fallback. Set it to `false` to restore the
pure-chunk behavior (the child must chunk long reports manually).

## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

### Compaction report detail

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

## Prompts, TTSR & A2A

The remaining user-file sections (all global scope):

```yaml
prompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file
  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."
ttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)
  enabled: true
  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard
  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once
a2a:                            # remote Agent2Agent endpoints
  servers:
    peer:
      url: https://peer.example:8080
      token: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value]}      # env-resolved at boot — never a literal secret
fabric:                         # host discovery announcements (read-only:
  capabilities:                 # written by hosts, never user-edited)
    - name: yoclip.render
      description: Render the open project to MP4
```

`a2a` servers are remote-only (a `url`, like remote MCP servers), so they
configure fine on process-less hosts. A `token` is an `\${ENV}` reference
resolved at boot; config `check`/`set` keep the token text literal, so an
unset variable surfaces when the agent boots, not as a config error.

## Settings hub

<!-- parity: /settings -->

`/settings` is an interactive hub over the surfaces above (provider, model,

## Example invocations

- `point project memory at ./memory` → Memory section: `config` op `set`,
  key `memory.projectPath`, value `./memory` (project file is the default
  scope — created minimal if missing), then `check`, then report live
  application.
- `switch us to provider X` → Provider & keys: `config` op `set` for
  `provider:` (and `baseUrl:`) in the user file — global scope is the
  default for these keys; report next-boot application and the `/provider`
  equivalent.

- `add custom provider Y and switch to it` → Provider & keys: `config` op
  `get customProviders`, `config` op `set customProviders <extended JSON
  list>` (see the config-tool section), then `set provider openai-completions`,
  `set model <entry modelId>`, `set baseUrl <entry baseUrl>`; verify with
  `check`, report next-boot application and the `/provider` equivalent.

## Output

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one
key — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with
`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for
the run), thinking deltas print dimmed and live like the TUI's, so ssh
sessions show the model's reasoning as it happens. The default `false`
keeps the interactive line-mode byte shape and prints a periodic
`… reasoning Ns` liveness line instead while a provider request sits
silent — the same waiting cadence the tool-liveness lines use
(`waiting.toolLivenessSeconds` / `toolLivenessTickSeconds`; `0` disables).

Since gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless
`fa -p` run streams thinking and text by default (the log is the UI, no
flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml
output:
  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default
```

Applies at next boot (the flag applies to its own run).

## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot
instruction files merge into the system prompt under a byte budget,
allocated leaf-first (deeper files win, issue #1761). Truncation is never
silent: the model sees a head excerpt plus an explicit
read-the-full-file instruction, a dropped file leaves a one-line
tombstone, and the user gets a boot notice per truncated/dropped file.
Tolerant parse: unknown keys surface as `[projectContext]` notes at boot,
never boot failures. `maxBytes: 0` disables the section entirely (no file
reads, fast boot):

```yaml
projectContext:
  maxBytes: 32768 # merged budget; 0 = section off, no file reads
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for
product/store links — the App Store banner in the web/macOS apps, the
CLI, and the fa1.dev site generator all resolve the same values, so a
link changes in ONE place. Defaults are baked in; only overrides are
written. Strict parse: a non-map section, a non-URL value, or a
non-boolean banner is a `ConfigException`; unknown keys become notes,
never failures:

```yaml
links:
  appstore: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163
  testflight: https://testflight.apple.com/join/En1eC9UK
  site: https://fa1.dev
  banner: true # false = no in-app App Store banner anywhere
```

`play:` (the Google Play release) stays ABSENT until the Android release
is live — every surface renders the Android slot as "coming soon" while
it is unset.

`banner: false` is the regression switch: the Get surface stays
byte-identical to the legacy UI. The section is user-file only (like
`tui:`/`fabric:`) and applies at next boot for the in-app banner; the
site renders the committed defaults (regen:
`dart run scripts/regen_site_store_block.dart`).

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

@@ -191,6 +191,157 @@ pinned expansions never hide (F8/#1379), hides are lossless appends
 continues visibly (`[resuming] continuing the turn on the compacted
 context`).
 
+### Soft window and honest overhead (gh-2411)
+
+The context window is a SOFT target — a slight overrun is accepted; an
+invisible user turn is not. Three rules, one basis:
+
+- **The newest real user turn never drops.** The turn and its pair
+  group are excluded from the checkpoint range and from every hide
+  candidate (real user text was already exempt). When a mechanical cut
+  has to land BEHIND the turn — the local trim valve's budget walk, or
+  a classic cut that splits the turn — the turn is CARRIED: the valve
+  re-homes it verbatim right after its `[context trimmed]` marker, and
+  the classic summary opens with the ask verbatim. A hard floor at the
+  turn was tried and rejected: it leaves a long tool-using turn with
+  nothing trimmable and kills the funnel backstop
+  (`lib/src/compaction/newest_user_turn.dart`).
+- **The overhead is priced as the provider bills it.** Every request
+  carries a fixed overhead — the system prompt and the tool schemas.
+  It is priced at 2.5 chars/token, not the transcript's 4 (measured on
+  the gh-2411 session: 65,561 overhead chars — 12,105 of system prompt
+  plus 34 tool schemas — were billed 24,126 provider tokens, 2.72
+  chars/token, where chars/4 priced 16,407, 32% under).
+  Per session the first valid provider `usage.input` calibrates the
+  estimate (`OverheadCalibration`, ratio clamped to [0.6, 4.0];
+  re-derived at resume from the last valid provider report anywhere in
+  the session — gh-2411 follow-up #5c) — it may LOWER an over-reading heuristic too (the
+  owner's live test: glm-5.3-flash billed 15,792 tokens where the
+  heuristic read 24,348, ratio 0.65) — and the ctx meter, the loop's
+  over-window guard and the compaction trigger all read that same
+  basis (`estimateRequestTokens`). The heuristic itself is a
+  per-provider average: before the first anchor lands the meter can be
+  off by that ratio.
+- **Soft window — no trim thrash, no unbounded growth.** When
+  `overhead + newest user turn ≥ window − reserve`, no trim can ever
+  reach the trigger. WHILE THE ESTIMATE IS UNDER THE WINDOW nothing is
+  trimmed: automatic compaction is skipped and the session is warned
+  ONCE per distinct warning text (a resumed session does not repeat it
+  at its first prompt): `context window {window} is below the fixed request overhead
+  ≈{overhead} tokens (estimated from the system prompt + tool schemas)
+  — raising the window or disabling tools is the only fix; automatic
+  compaction is skipped while the context stays under the window`. AT OR OVER THE WINDOW the
+  request is simply over the window: the automatic pass is the
+  hide-only, LM-free relief (the same one the loop guard runs — the
+  newest user turn is still carried verbatim), a pass that frees
+  nothing re-runs only after the transcript changed, and the loop's
+  over-window guard keeps its stop. ONE predicate decides both sides —
+  `softWindowSkip`: the regime AND `estimate < window`
+  (`lib/src/compaction/soft_window.dart`). Skipping over the window as
+  well was the first cut; the owner's live test grew a session to 114%
+  with no pass ever running.

request overhead ≈21000 + the newest user turn ≈6000 already reach it
